naming_clarity.reason: Title and body stay in stakeholder vocabulary (safety engineer, driver, workshop, test bench, safe window); thermal runaway is standard battery-domain terminology a non-implementer stakeholder can confirm.

no_mechanism_leak.reason: No class, function, module, table, internal endpoint or technology choice appears; high-voltage circuit and terminals are physical domain objects, and no contactor, sensor or software construct is named.

parent_fit.reason: user_story is the root stage of this project V and the need carries no outgoing parent link, so per the pack scoring guide this axis is fully met by default.

single_user_capability.reason: One capability throughout: remove the pack from the high-voltage circuit when any cell leaves its safe voltage, current or temperature window. The driver warning, stored fault entry, latch-until-cleared and bench measurement are all facets of that same disconnect event, and the other two pack capabilities are explicitly scoped out.

user_observable.reason: Four external observation points are named: driver battery warning plus loss of drive power, a workshop fault entry naming the cell and the limit crossed, high-voltage terminals measurably dead on a test bench within a bounded reaction time, and the pack staying disconnected until a technician clears the fault.

summary: Root user story describing one protective-disconnect capability in externally observable terms, with no implementation constructs named. Full marks on all five axes (10/10).
